$comment: Curated free learning resources. Every URL is checked by `npm run verify:links`, which writes link-check.json. Do not add ratings or time estimates: only facts we can verify. `check` is text that must appear on the page for the link to count as verified.

resources.title: Elements of AI
resources.summary: A free online introduction to artificial intelligence for non-experts: what AI is, what it can and cannot do, and how it affects society. No maths or programming needed.
resources.accessibility: Text-based course offered in many languages.

resources.title: Ethics of AI
resources.summary: An open online course on the ethical questions raised by AI, such as fairness, transparency, accountability and human rights.

resources.title: AI Fluency: Framework and foundations
resources.summary: Learn to work with AI effectively and responsibly using a four-part framework: delegation, description, discernment and diligence. Works with any AI assistant.

resources.title: AI capabilities and limitations
resources.summary: Build an accurate picture of how language models work — next-token prediction, knowledge, working memory and context limits — so you know when to trust them.

resources.title: Introduction to AI concepts
resources.summary: A short module covering the main kinds of AI workloads — generative AI, computer vision, speech, language and information extraction — and responsible AI basics.
resources.paidExtras: Microsoft certification exams are paid and separate.

resources.title: AI for Beginners
resources.summary: An open curriculum of lessons and labs covering symbolic AI, neural networks, computer vision and natural language processing, with Python notebooks.

resources.title: What is artificial intelligence (AI)?
resources.summary: A plain-language explainer of AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI, and how they relate.

resources.title: What is machine learning?
resources.summary: An overview of how machine learning works, the main learning approaches and common uses.

resources.title: What is generative AI?
resources.summary: How generative AI creates text, images and code, where businesses use it, and its risks.

resources.title: Neural networks (video series)
resources.summary: Animated lessons that build intuition for how neural networks learn, from gradient descent and backpropagation to transformers.
resources.accessibility: Video lessons with written versions on the site.

resources.title: But what is a GPT?
resources.summary: A visual introduction to transformers, the architecture behind large language models.

resources.title: A Neural Network Playground
resources.summary: Train a small neural network in your browser and watch how layers, neurons and learning rate change what it learns.

resources.title: Intro to Large Language Models
resources.summary: A general-audience talk on what large language models are, how they are trained, and their security challenges.

resources.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
resources.summary: Build neural networks from scratch in code, ending with a GPT-style language model.

resources.title: Prompt engineering overview
resources.summary: Practical techniques for clear prompts: being specific, giving examples, structuring with tags, and letting the model think step by step.
resources.paidExtras: Trying the techniques through the API is billed; reading is free.

resources.title: Prompt engineering guide
resources.summary: Strategies for getting better results from language models, with examples of instructions, context and formatting.
resources.paidExtras: Trying the techniques through the API is billed; reading is free.

resources.title: Prompt design strategies
resources.summary: Google's guide to writing prompts: clear instructions, few-shot examples, adding context and breaking down tasks.

resources.title: Learn Prompting
resources.summary: An open guide to prompting, from the basics to advanced techniques and prompt-injection risks.
resources.paidExtras: Some courses on the site are paid.

resources.title: Prompt Engineering Guide
resources.summary: A reference to prompting techniques such as chain-of-thought, retrieval-augmented generation and agents, with links to the research behind them.

resources.title: OpenAI Cookbook
resources.summary: Example code for common tasks with language-model APIs: retrieval, embeddings, function calling and evaluation.
resources.paidExtras: Running the examples calls paid APIs.

resources.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
resources.summary: A short, non-technical introduction to what machine learning is and the kinds of problems it solves.

resources.title: Machine Learning Crash Course
resources.summary: Video lectures, interactive visualizations and exercises covering regression, classification, data, neural networks and responsible ML.

resources.title: Python
resources.summary: Short hands-on lessons on Python fundamentals, with exercises in the browser.

resources.title: Intro to Machine Learning
resources.summary: Build your first models with decision trees and random forests on real data, with exercises in the browser.

resources.title: Machine Learning for Beginners
resources.summary: An open curriculum on classic machine learning — regression, classification, clustering, NLP and time series — using Scikit-learn.

resources.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
resources.summary: A code-first course that has you training deep learning models for vision, text and tabular data from the first lesson.
resources.paidExtras: Cloud GPUs can cost money, though free options are covered.
prerequisites: About a year of coding experience, ideally Python

resources.title: LLM Course
resources.summary: Learn how transformer language models work and how to use, fine-tune and share them with the Hugging Face libraries.

resources.title: AI Agents Course
resources.summary: Learn how AI agents combine models with tools and planning, and build agents with popular open-source frameworks.

resources.title: Diffusion Models Course
resources.summary: Theory and code for the diffusion models behind image generation, including training and fine-tuning your own.

resources.title: Introduction to Generative AI
resources.summary: A short introductory course explaining what generative AI is, how it is used and how it differs from traditional machine learning.

resources.title: Generative AI for Beginners
resources.summary: Lessons on building generative AI applications: prompting, chat and search apps, image generation, retrieval and responsible use.
resources.paidExtras: Code lessons need access to a model API, which may cost money.
prerequisites: Basic Python or TypeScript for the code lessons

resources.title: The Illustrated Transformer
resources.summary: A visual, step-by-step explanation of the transformer architecture and self-attention.

resources.title: Transformer Explainer
resources.summary: An interactive visualization that runs a small GPT-2 model in your browser so you can see how each part of a transformer works.

resources.title: CNN Explainer
resources.summary: An interactive visualization of how a convolutional neural network classifies images.

resources.title: Attention Is All You Need
resources.summary: The 2017 research paper that introduced the transformer architecture.

resources.title: Distill (archive)
resources.summary: Interactive research articles explaining machine learning ideas. The journal is on hiatus; its archive remains available.

resources.title: Getting started with scikit-learn
resources.summary: The official introduction to fitting, predicting, preprocessing and evaluating models with scikit-learn.

resources.title: PyTorch Tutorials
resources.summary: Official tutorials covering tensors, training loops, vision, text and deployment.

resources.title: TensorFlow Tutorials
resources.summary: Official notebooks for beginners and experts, runnable in the browser with Google Colab.

resources.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
resources.publisher: James, Witten, Hastie, Tibshirani and Taylor
resources.summary: A widely used textbook on regression, classification, resampling, trees and more, with Python and R editions. The PDF is free from the authors' site.

resources.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
resources.summary: The linear algebra, calculus and probability behind machine learning. The PDF is free from the book's site.

resources.title: Dive into Deep Learning
resources.summary: An interactive book that teaches deep learning with runnable code alongside the maths.

resources.title: Deep Learning
resources.summary: A comprehensive textbook on the theory of deep learning, free to read online.

resources.title: Introduction to Machine Learning (6.036)
resources.summary: MIT's undergraduate introduction to machine learning, with lecture videos, notes and exercises.

resources.title: Introduction to Deep Learning (6.S191)
resources.summary: MIT's introductory deep learning course, with lecture videos, slides and software labs.

resources.title: Machine Learning (CS229)
resources.summary: Recorded lectures, handouts and assignments from Stanford's machine learning course taught by Andrew Ng.

resources.title: CS50's Introduction to Artificial Intelligence with Python
resources.summary: Lectures and projects on search, knowledge, uncertainty, optimization, machine learning, neural networks and language.
resources.paidExtras: A verified certificate through edX costs extra.

resources.title: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science
resources.summary: Harvard's introduction to computer science and programming, from C to Python, SQL and web development.
resources.paidExtras: A verified certificate through edX costs extra.

resources.title: The Python Tutorial
resources.summary: The official, thorough introduction to the Python language.

resources.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
resources.summary: A practical beginner's book on using Python to automate everyday tasks with files, spreadsheets, PDFs and the web. Free to read online.
resources.paidExtras: Print and e-book editions are sold separately.

resources.title: freeCodeCamp curriculum
resources.summary: A free, project-based curriculum covering web development, JavaScript, Python and more, with certifications.

resources.title: The Odin Project
resources.summary: An open-source full-stack web development curriculum built around real projects.

resources.title: Learn web development
resources.summary: Mozilla's structured guide to HTML, CSS, JavaScript and accessibility for beginners.
resources.accessibility: Covers accessible web development as a core topic.

resources.title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
resources.summary: The first global standard on AI ethics, adopted by UNESCO member states, setting out values and policy actions.

resources.title: OECD AI Principles
resources.summary: Internationally agreed principles for trustworthy AI and recommendations for policy makers.

resources.title: AI Risk Management Framework
resources.summary: A voluntary framework to help organisations identify, measure and manage risks from AI systems, with a companion playbook.

resources.title: People + AI Guidebook
resources.summary: Practical guidance for designing human-centred AI products: user needs, trust, explanations, feedback and errors.

resources.title: Guidance on AI and data protection
resources.summary: How data protection law applies to AI systems that process personal data: fairness, transparency, security and individual rights.

resources.title: AI Playbook for the UK Government
resources.summary: Principles and practical guidance for using AI safely and effectively in public-sector organisations; much of it applies to any organisation.

resources.title: Guidance for generative AI in education and research
resources.check: generative AI in education and research
resources.summary: Global guidance on using generative AI in education and research in ways that protect human agency, privacy and academic integrity.

resources.title: How do I cite generative AI in MLA style?
resources.summary: Official MLA advice on citing text, images and other content created with AI tools.

resources.title: Generative AI in Academic Writing
resources.publisher: The Writing Center, UNC Chapel Hill
resources.summary: Guidance for students on when and how AI tools can support writing, their limits, and keeping your own voice and integrity.

resources.title: Research and Citation Resources
resources.summary: How to find, evaluate and cite sources, with guides to APA, MLA and Chicago styles — essential for checking what AI tools tell you.

resources.title: AI Pedagogy Project
resources.summary: Assignments and guides from educators for teaching critically with and about AI.

resources.title: AI lessons and activities
resources.summary: Lessons, videos and activities that teach students how AI works and how to use it responsibly.

resources.title: Day of AI curriculum
resources.summary: Free AI literacy lessons for school students, designed for teachers with no AI background.

resources.title: AI Literacy Lessons for Grades K–12
resources.summary: Short lessons for teachers and families on what AI is, how it can be wrong, and using it fairly and safely.

resources.title: Teachable Machine
resources.summary: Train a simple image, sound or pose model in your browser with no code, to see how machine learning learns from examples.

resources.title: Machine Learning for Kids
resources.summary: Hands-on projects where children train models and use them in Scratch, App Inventor or Python.

resources.title: AI for small business
resources.summary: An overview of how small businesses can use AI, with key terms, benefits and risks to weigh.

resources.title: Transform your business with AI
resources.summary: A learning path for business decision makers on AI strategy, generative AI opportunities and responsible adoption. Some modules refer to Microsoft products.

resources.title: IBM SkillsBuild
resources.summary: Free courses on AI, data and technology skills for adult learners, students and job seekers, with digital credentials.

paths.title: AI fundamentals
paths.audience: Anyone curious about AI. No maths or coding needed.
paths.description: Understand what AI is, how today's systems learn, what they can and cannot do, and how to use them well.

steps.why: A gentle, well-structured first course on what AI is.
Untangles AI, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI.
Tour of the main kinds of AI workloads you will meet.
See a neural network learn, right in your browser.
Visual intuition for how neural networks train.
How large language models are made, for a general audience.
Know when to trust a model and when to check.
Turn understanding into good everyday habits with any assistant.

paths.title: Prompt engineering
paths.audience: Anyone who uses AI chat tools for work or study.
paths.description: Write clearer prompts, give the right context, and check results — techniques that work across providers.

steps.why: A framework for deciding what to delegate and how to describe it.
Core strategies with concrete examples.
Techniques like examples, structure and step-by-step thinking.
Few-shot examples, context and breaking down tasks.
From basics to prompt-injection risks.
Reference for advanced techniques and the research behind them.

paths.title: AI for students
paths.audience: Secondary-school and university students, and the teachers who support them.
paths.description: Learn how AI works, try it hands-on, and use it honestly in your coursework.

steps.why: Short lessons and activities on how AI works.
Train your own model with no code.
A complete, free introductory course.
When AI helps your writing, and when it gets in the way.
How to credit AI tools in your work.
Check sources instead of trusting AI answers.
Start programming with short, hands-on lessons.
A university-level next step once you can code.

paths.title: Writing and research with AI
paths.description: Use AI to support — not replace — your thinking, check facts against real sources, and cite AI use properly.

steps.why: Why models can sound confident and still be wrong.
Practical boundaries for AI in academic writing.
Find, evaluate and cite sources.
Cite AI-generated content correctly.
Ask for structure, sources and critique rather than finished text.
The bigger picture on integrity and human agency.
Ideas from educators on critical, creative AI use.

paths.title: AI for small businesses
paths.audience: Owners and staff of small businesses and non-profits.
paths.description: Find practical uses for AI, adopt it responsibly, and protect customer data.

steps.why: Plain overview of benefits and risks for small firms.
What generative AI can do for a business.
Habits for delegating work to AI effectively.
Planning an AI strategy and adoption.
Automate repetitive office tasks yourself.
Keep customer data safe and lawful.
Short principles for trustworthy AI use.
A structured way to think about AI risks.
Free courses for you and your staff.

paths.title: Programming for AI
paths.audience: Beginners learning to code, and developers who want to add AI to their apps.
paths.description: Learn to program, then build applications that use AI models.

steps.why: A rigorous, friendly introduction to programming.
Python is the main language of AI tooling.
Practise Python on useful, real tasks.
The web basics most AI apps are built on.
Build chat, search and image apps step by step.
Prompts are part of your code — write them well.
Working examples of retrieval, tools and evaluation.
Build agents that combine models and tools.

paths.title: Generative AI
paths.audience: People who want to understand how today's generative models work.
paths.description: From a first explanation to the transformer architecture and building with open models.

steps.why: The big picture of large language models.
How generative AI differs from traditional ML.
Hands-on lessons building generative apps.
Visual intuition for transformers.
Step-by-step walk through self-attention.
Poke at a real GPT-2 running in your browser.
Use, fine-tune and share open models.
How image generators work.
Read the original transformer paper.

paths.title: Responsible AI
paths.audience: Everyone who builds, buys or uses AI.
paths.description: Fairness, transparency, privacy and accountability — the principles and the practical frameworks.

steps.why: A full course on the ethical questions.
The global standard on AI ethics.
Concise international principles.
Design AI products people can trust.
Manage AI risk in practice.
Privacy and data protection in AI systems.
Real-world guidance for organisations.
Teach responsible AI use to young people.

Build your first models on real data.
Core concepts with interactive exercises.

MIT's deep learning lectures and labs.
